title: Astronavigation for yachtsmen: sextant, sun sights and the noon latitude
h1: Finding your position by the sun and stars
lead: Far from land with the electronics down, a sextant, an accurate watch and an almanac still tell you where you are. This guide explains celestial navigation at Yachtmaster Ocean level, from taking a sun sight to the noon latitude and a running fix.
description: Celestial navigation for yacht skippers: the sextant and index error, time, circles of equal altitude, altitude corrections, the intercept method, the noon sight, running fixes, Polaris, star sights and accuracy.
summary: Check the index error before every set of sights, and time each sight to the second in UT.
An error of 4 seconds in your time puts your position about a mile out east or west at the equator.
In the intercept method, if the observed altitude is greater than the calculated one, the intercept is towards the body.
A noon sight gives your latitude directly, and a morning sun sight crossed with it gives a running fix.
